sentences.text:
Petitioner is present before this Court and has been identified by his counsel Mr. Amitesh Pandey,
Advocate and Investigating Officer (IO) from Police Station Paharganj, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 got married on 06.12.2014 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
Two children were born out of the said wedlock.
It is stated that due to some misunderstanding and temperamental differences, both the parties started residing separately since 17.12.2019.

It is stated that on the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 318/2020 registered at Police Station Paharganj, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/506/323/34/509/354/354A of IPC against the petitioner.
During pendency of the case, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes vide Panchayati Faisla/Settlement Deed dated 16.03.2023 and had dissolved their marriage.

7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Panchayati Faisla/Settlement Deed dated 16.03.2023 and has been signed by all the parties and affidavits showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 19:39:24 8.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no.1 and other family members.

9. As per settlement, petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 5,50,000/- to respondent no. 2 in four instalments in the following manner:
a.
First installment of Rs.2,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 vide DD No. 059288 dated 18.02.2023.

b. Second installment of Rs.1,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of Second motion.
c. Third installment of Rs.1,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 vide Demand Draft.
c. Fourth/Final instalment of Rs.1,00,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Hon'ble High Court at New Delhi.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the above mentioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
